summary: Helena National Forest tower on Avalanche Butte, listed as gone and abandoned in the 1950s; a 1958 survey marker is the only later site record found.

facts.design: 10-ft wooden tower; firelookout.com asks whether a cab was added later
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; Kemnow's page shows 'Removed' beside 'National Geodetic Survey' with no date and no explanation

events.note: Portable short-wave radio set installed at 'Avalanche Mountain', per a July 9, 1936 Independent Record notice quoted by Kemnow; the quoted sentence does not mention a tower
Source says only 'Abandoned 1950s'; 1950 stands in for that decade and is not a dated record
USGS survey description: station on the highest point, on the Broadwater-Meagher county line, at the site of an abandoned Forest Service observation point

evidence.supports: About 28 miles northeast of Helena, Helena National Forest
Entry opens with the 1930s and 'camp', describes 10-ft wooden tower, cab question, abandoned 1950s
evidence.quote: 1930s: camp. 10' wooden tower with cab added later? Abandoned 1950s.

evidence.supports: 1936 radio installation notice quoted by Kemnow, measured from Townsend
evidence.quote: A portable short wave radio set was installed at Avalanche Mountain, 30 miles northeast of Townsend.

evidence.supports: 'Removed' beside 'National Geodetic Survey', with no date or explanation

notes_for_editor: Build date and builder not established: firelookout.com's entry reads '1930s: camp.' and asks whether a cab was added later, so no built event is recorded. The 1950 abandonment year is a placeholder for 'Abandoned 1950s'. Elevation 7,701 ft (firelookout.com) is now recorded as elevation_ft. The '10-ft' tower is not converted to height_m because the source does not say whether it is tower height or another dimension. The 1936 radio item names 'Avalanche Mountain' and a Townsend reference point; the story says the link to this tower rests on Kemnow's filing. Kemnow's 'Removed' sits beside 'National Geodetic Survey' with no date or explanation, so the story does not treat it as the tower's own status. WebSearch found a Helena-area wildfire near Avalanche Gulch with no year in the excerpts; it is not the lookout and was not used.
